reviews.review:
I'm quite surprised how amazing this game is.

The single player was one hell of a ride. Extremely enjoyable ride. Ride full of slashing limbs and making big holes in torsos and vaporizing hundreds and thousands (definitely thousands) of green skins and heretics.

The combat mechanics are nothing new, but they are well polished and the killing enemies is satisfactory. The melee fighting in large groups of foes could take some work because your character starts to stutter when he is being hit from every possible side and angle. But it's still better than being surrounded by group of enemies and being attacked only by one at a time (ehm ehm AC ehm ehm). Shooting experience is also really good, as is the feeling of watching explosion of blood after a bolt from your weapon penetrates the body of your target. The execution mode which regenerates health by finishing enemies has nice range of incredibly good looking animations.

The weapon progression is slow but steady. You have 4 different melee weapons and 10 ranged weapons at your disposal. Through out the game you'll find fury seals (something like a berserker mode) which will upgrade your ability. But only with something incremental as longer fury time, or regenerating HP by inflicting damage. Those are nice things to have, but there could be something more interesting gameplay wise. The steady progression comes to a halt few chapters before the end of the game, which is kinda sad. There are also few instances where you have a jetpack, whit which you can propel yourself up into the air, find a group of foes and fall down on them dealing massive damage, stunning them and looking at the awesome shockwave.

The level design isn't anything special or even good. It's a corridor with a lot of curves and vertical traverses. But even though  it isn't great from gameplay point of view, the game has an amazing atmosphere. I love postapo and I could feel it everywhere I've went. It was awesome, the heavy feeling that this world is doomed and that there is no hope for civilians. And that I'm here to help however I can, fighting "alone" against the never ending hordes. This is nicely complemented by a atmospheric soundtrack. 

The story isn't something special, it's your generic shooter story with a villain and wanna be twist waiting for you somewhere. But I would say that for a WH40k fan it has to be really enjoyable. It's a game that is suppose to be pure fun and relax, not something to think about, so I don't see a problem with the story line. The only weak point was the final boss fight which was a dull sequence of the same QTEs over and over again.

There isn't anyone in the multi player right now which is sad. Because when I've played it with friends few years ago it was great fun. There are some basic modes like versus (team against team) or you can play some parts of the story (I don't think it's the whole story, but I can't remember) with a group of friends.

My conclusion is that it's a great entertaining game, pure fun from killing thousands of enemies and I can recommend it to everyone.

8.7/10 (I like the number 7)

WH40K Space Marine is a 3rd person combat game that has you, as Ultramarine Captain Titus, wade your way using guns, grenades, and melee weapons through enemies of the Imperium, such as (but not limited to) the Orks. The game starts with space sensors detecting Ork ships approaching Forge World Graia and the only ones in range to respond in time was Captain Titus, along with Sergeant Sidonus, and rookie Tech Marine Leandros. They wade their way into battle, fighting their way through Ork lines to reach the Imperial Guard on the surface, and accomplished several missions such as disabling the space cannon captured by the Orks, as well as reach Inquisitor Drogan who claimed to have a weapon that can wipe the Orks off the planet, only to discover an even greater threat hiding in the wings...

Captain Titus is a veteran fighter and knows all the moves, including bashing, slicing, and more, as well as seamlessly switching between gunplay and melee. On the other hand, there are tons of Orks around, various types, from shooters to melee to minibosses to true level bosses. 

Enemies can be shot or blasted with grenades, but the most visceral way of dispatching enemies is with melee, as you will yield vibroblade, power axe, and even shockhammer into combat. Enemies can also be stunned THEN "fatalized" with a fatality / execution, which is the only way for you to regain health. 

There are occasional segments that involve a rocket pack, for you to jump up and bypass many walls, ledges, and such. Yet others have you use fixed heavy guns against enemies, and Ork gunships, and even rip off the heavy guns and use them as limited-ammo miniguns the enemies in your way. Grenades can be used to flush enemies out of cover. And there are various types of guns, from short-range stormers to ultra-long sniper rifles. 

The levels are detailed, and characters are very nicely digitized. There are hidden collectibles you can find all around the levels that will unlock bonus powers, and new eapons and abilities are unlocked at a steady pace. 

The moves are exquisite, with the different melee weapons were all wielded with very different combat styles. Vibroblades are stabbed and swung, but axes and hammers are swung hard and knock enemies back, and each weapon has different set of pros and cons, such as power vs. swing speed vs. weapon change speed. 

You don't always fight alone. Sometimes your fellow ultramarines are on your side, while others have you fighting alongside the Imperial Guards. yet other time you will find yourself watching the other two factions fight and you decide who should be your target. 

The game sometimes gets extremely frustrating when it gives you a gunship that is highly resistant against the fire you're putting out, WHILE the gunship drops enemies behind you, yet on other levels the game is perfectly balanced, not too easy so it's no longer a challenge, but never hard enough to make you want to rage quit. 

All in all, if you like WH40K and/or 3rd person combat games that involves no jumping, you should give this a try.

I really like this game, but then, I am a 40K fanboy. 

The game is a linear, point to point slaughter fest. A lot of the negative reviews mention it is repetitive it is. Then again so is every shooter in recent years. 

What the game does have is faithful to the lore art and information, great sound effects and a combat system that seamlessly switches between ranged combat and melee. The combat is visceral and very satisfying.  Despite being nearly four years old the engine has aged well.

It is, I find amusing, that some reviews talk about the story being basic when the vast majority of games available are even worse and titles with grander production values fair worse. This game isn't Deus Ex and nor is it Wolfenstein Old Blood, i,e the only two shooters I can remember that have a good campaign.  It is satisfying, fit for purpose and gives you an excuse to kill lots of things. 

There are a number of enemy unit types in the game and most of the core Ork units are there, boyz, nobz, weirdboyz, gretchin, ard boyz and the warboss. Chaos units are fairly limited to psyers, cultist, tactical and devestator marines, champions and Khorne bloodletters. 

The campaign is the usual 7-8 hours odd depending on how much time you spend looking for things and difficulty you play on. This is pretty much standard to most Single Player games. 

The game is very well presented and polished. Negative reviews mention a number of issues, AI, geometry and scripting errors and I've yet to come across any issues, nada not one. 

One down side is the multiplayer which can be difficult to find games on, although it does have a large amount of customisation it could do with more variety. Even the horde mode is quite limited and perhaps should have went down the Dawn of War 2 route and allowed players to also play as Orks and Imperial Guard. 

I've gifted copies to friends and family to try and drag them into the game. 

Space Marine is game I will play again and again, it is the perfect game to just to unwind with, slaughter a few Orks and move on.
